title: Livestream Duration, Witness and the 100,000-Hour Threshold
status: project-supplied duration claim plus externally dated Minecraft anchor
purpose: Relate the project's approximately 112,542-hour livestream claim to the older 100,000-hour spiral motif without treating the claim as independently verified until platform logs or primary records are assembled.

claims.speaker_description: Tim says he is not a content creator but the world's greatest 'non-tent creator' / non-content creator; preserve the phrase as project self-description and wordplay.
claims.continuity_claim: The livestreaming continuum is described as beginning with the Son around the Minecraft rail/minecart update and continuing through the later Tim identity.
claims.verification_status: The total hours and Son-to-Tim continuity are project-supplied claims requiring platform/archive verification for documentary status.

minecraft_anchor.documented_change: Beta 1.5 added detector rails and powered/booster rails and is a clear public minecart/rail update anchor.
minecraft_anchor.project_claim: The Son started streaming around this rail/minecart update; this linkage is not independently established by the Minecraft release record itself.

interpretation.100000_hour_spiral: The existing project treats 100,000 hours as a memetic/symbolic threshold for long-duration transformation rather than a scientific law.
interpretation.112542_hour_meaning: If the claimed total is accurate, the public-witness motif has passed beyond the symbolic threshold by more than twelve thousand hours, so 100,000 functions as an exceeded landmark rather than an endpoint.
interpretation.witness_model: Livestreaming becomes less like isolated content production and more like accumulated public presence: repetition, memory, archive, observation and continuity across identity stages.
interpretation.non_content_creator_paradox: The refusal of 'content creator' language reframes the stream as existence/witness rather than production. The archive should preserve this as self-description, not assume audiences or platforms necessarily share that interpretation.
interpretation.continuity_question: If Son-era and Tim-era hours are combined, the duration becomes a continuity measure across the project's personhood transformation. To split the hours between Son and Tim accurately, dated stream logs are required.

do_not_infer: Do not assume 112,542 hours means a person was awake on camera for every counted hour; continuous streams can include sleep, absence or unattended broadcast time.
Do not back-calculate the date on which 100,000 hours was crossed unless actual cumulative stream logs are available.
Do not treat the Minecraft update as evidence that the Son caused the game update; it is only the project's chosen chronological anchor.
research_tasks: Acquire platform/channel logs and archived broadcast timestamps.
Define whether simultaneous broadcasts count once or multiple times.
Separate live-on-camera, live-stream-active and archived-video hours.
Partition the timeline into Son-era, transition-era and Tim-era hours only when dated evidence permits.
Locate the earliest use of the 10,000-hour and 100,000-hour motifs and compare them with the actual cumulative stream total.
